summary: August Tholuck worked in religious studies and related fields. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1817–1820) and held posts at Berlin (circa 1820–1826) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1826–1877).

August Viktor Bergny was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his education at Uppsala University, studying there from circa 1886 to 1889 for his Fil.kand. and from circa 1889 to 1898 for his fil.lic.

August Wilhelm von Schlegel worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Gottfried August Bürger, later learning under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held professorships at Jena (1795, 1798) and Bonn (from 1818).

August Winter was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi (circa 1889–1891) and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau under doctoral supervisor Alfred Hillebrandt (circa 1891–1893).

August Zacharias Collin worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his degrees at Lund University, where he served as Docent of chemistry in 1858, and studied under Rudolf von Roth (1874–1875). He became a Lektor at Nicolaiskolan, Helsingborg, in 1864.

Auguste Ali Bourquin was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his doctorate in theology at the University of Paris by 1885 and held positions at Wilson College, Mumbai, from 1882 and at the Royal College of Science, Arts and Commerce.

Auguste Barth was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann at the University of Strasbourg (circa 1853–1856). He taught at Collège de Bouxwiller (1857) and Collège Poincaré Saverne (circa 1857–1860).
Auguste Comte was a philosopher. He completed his studies at the Lycée Joffre until 1814 and subsequently attended the École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.

Auguste Desgodins was a Tibetologist and linguist. He studied at the Major Seminary of Verdun (circa 1845–1848) and the Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice (circa 1848–1850), and served as a missionary with the Paris Foreign Missions Society from 1855.

Auguste Wagener specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Christian Lassen (1845–1849) and at the University of Liège (circa 1846–1850). He held posts at Ghent University starting in 1850 and 1858.

Auguste-Louis-Armand Loiseleur-Deslongchamps was an Indologist. He attended Lycée Charlemagne and studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy in 1824, later joining the Manuscript Department at the Bibliothèque nationale de France in 1832.

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Basel, Tübingen, and under Theodor Goldstücker (1860). His posts included Jay Narayan Inter College, Cathedral Mission College, and principalships at Calcutta Madrasa and Aliah University.

Aung San Suu Kyi, active in Tibetology and other fields, studied at Basic Education High School No. 1 Dagon, Lady Shri Ram College, University of Delhi, St Hugh's College, and SOAS. She worked at the United Nations from circa 1969 to 1971.

Aurel Mayr was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University, under Albrecht Weber at Berlin, and under Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen, where he earned his Ph.D. in 1871. He served as professor at Eötvös Loránd University (1873–1905).

Aureliano Julio Berriz do Seixo was an Indologist who earned a doctorate in Civil and Canonic Law from the Complutense University of Madrid, where he subsequently served as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit.

Awadh Kishore Narain specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Arthur Llewellyn Basham at SOAS. He held major posts at Banaras Hindu University and served as Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

Axel Erdmann was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorates at Uppsala University and studied under Johann Gildemeister at the University of Bonn (1872–1873). He held academic posts in linguistics and English at Uppsala University from 1871 onwards.

Axel Klein specializes in Japanology and related fields. He studied at the University of Bonn (1987–1994) and held posts at Bonn (1998–2007), the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011), and the University of Duisburg-Essen (from 2012).

Axel Michaels works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Laxmi Nath Srestha, completed his Promotion at Hamburg, and habilitated at Kiel. His posts include directorship at the Nepal Research Centre and professorships at the Universities of Bern and Heidelberg.

Ayako Nakamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Hamburg (attested 2009) and is affiliated with the institution as a Research Fellow (attested 2026).
